meta.title: BRCAPath-Rx Stage 2 Confounding Demo
meta.subtitle: A click-through tutorial showing how unfair treated-vs-untreated comparisons can create false treatment stories.
meta.completed_case_badge: Only one real completed causal case so far
meta.completed_case_label: ER-positive METABRIC | hormone therapy YES vs NO | overall survival

tiny_idea.title: One tiny confounding idea
tiny_idea.setup: If students with tutors score lower, that does not prove tutors are harmful.
tiny_idea.wrong: Quick but wrong: tutors must have made them worse.
tiny_idea.better: Better: the weaker students were more likely to get tutors, so the tutor group started off behind.

fictional_cases.name: Illustration: hormone therapy
fictional_cases.treated_profile: Older on average, later stage, more positive lymph nodes
fictional_cases.untreated_profile: Younger on average, earlier stage, fewer positive lymph nodes
fictional_cases.wrong: The therapy looks harmful because the treated group did worse.
fictional_cases.better: The treated group already started with worse prognosis, so the crude comparison is unfair.

fictional_cases.name: Illustration: chemotherapy
fictional_cases.treated_profile: More advanced disease and more aggressive subtype mix
fictional_cases.untreated_profile: Milder disease and healthier subtype mix
fictional_cases.wrong: Chemotherapy looks harmful because the treated group had worse outcomes.
fictional_cases.better: The treated patients were more advanced to begin with, so the raw outcome gap is confounded.

fictional_cases.name: Illustration: radiotherapy
fictional_cases.treated_profile: More nodal involvement and more local disease burden
fictional_cases.untreated_profile: Less nodal involvement and lower local burden
fictional_cases.wrong: Radiotherapy looks harmful because the treated group looked worse overall.
fictional_cases.better: The treated group had more baseline risk, so treatment choice and prognosis were tangled together.

simulator.title: Confounding simulator
simulator.description: Switch on baseline differences in the treated group and watch the naive conclusion change even though the toy treatment itself is not helping or harming anyone here.

views.title: Before adjustment: the groups were not similar at baseline
views.text: The treated and untreated patients differed strongly in stage, nodal burden, age, menopausal state, and subtype mix.

views.title: The first raw comparison made hormone therapy look harmful
views.text: That crude result is descriptive only. It blends treatment with baseline prognosis.

views.title: After overlap weighting, measured balance improved sharply
views.text: That means the comparison became much fairer on the baseline variables we were able to measure.

views.title: The estimate moved toward about 1.00 after adjustment
views.text: That big shift tells us the naive comparison was misleading. It does not prove the final treatment effect.

overlap_figure.title: Overlap weighting focuses on comparable patients
overlap_figure.text: Patients in the overlap middle get more influence than extreme patients who almost certainly would or would not have been treated.

methods.name: Overlap weighting
methods.problem: Treated and untreated patients overlap only partly.
methods.helps: It gives more weight to patients who realistically could have gone either way.
methods.cannot: It still cannot fix confounders that were never measured.

methods.name: Propensity score matching
methods.problem: A crude comparison mixes together patients who were not similar at baseline.
methods.helps: It tries to pair more similar treated and untreated patients before comparing outcomes.
methods.cannot: It can discard many patients and still cannot remove hidden confounding.

future_candidates.name: Chemotherapy questions
future_candidates.why_next: Potentially important, but the treatment sorting looked stronger and overlap was weaker in the earlier screening step.

future_candidates.name: Radiotherapy questions
future_candidates.why_next: Potentially important, but local treatment choice is tightly entangled with surgery patterns and disease burden.

future_candidates.name: Subtype-specific treatment questions
future_candidates.why_next: Worth exploring only after a separate treatment audit confirms enough overlap, events, and confounder support.

ai_demo.without_adjustment: Without adjustment, the AI may learn a false pattern like 'treatment looks harmful' only because sicker patients were more likely to receive it.
ai_demo.with_adjustment: With adjustment, we try to give the model a cleaner treatment signal by reducing unfair baseline differences.
ai_demo.future_work: This multi-treatment recommendation logic is future Stage 2 work, not a completed system yet.

limitations: Only one real treatment-effect case is completed so far.
This is still observational data, not a randomized trial.
Adjustment helps, but it does not magically prove causality.
Important confounders are still missing, including comorbidity, adherence, exact regimen, and treatment-era detail.
say_aloud: This demo first shows how unfair group differences can create a false treatment story, then lets us click through the one real completed case study, and finally shows which treatment questions could be studied next without pretending they are already finished.
